A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ACE research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on N-Body simulations, QM9, ModelNet40, and CMU MoCap, including performance, training dynamics, sample efficiency, and robustness results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds N-Body ablations and a synthetic 2D symmetry-mismatch experiment.

M1.justification: The homotopic architecture, equality and resilient objectives, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The new pseudocode and spectral-normalization discussion document implementation and scale control; they do not establish a revision of the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: The four existing benchmark domains remain. Appendix A.4 adds a limited synthetic 2D image-mapping scenario: square-to-square, square-to-rectangle, and square-to-nonsymmetric targets under an imposed C4 symmetry.

E2.justification: The new 2D experiment evaluates a strictly C4-equivariant CNN without ACE against its ACE counterpart. Comparator membership in the retained main experiments is unchanged; the cited relaxed group-convolution approach is discussed but not evaluated in this new comparison.

E3.justification: New controlled experiments compare gamma initialization at zero versus one and sweep six dual learning rates on 1,000 N-Body samples with the primal rate fixed at 9×10^-4. Existing splits and main hyperparameter grids remain unchanged. The newly stated 300-point ModelNet40 input resolution is a disclosure, not an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2–A.4 substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's training-dynamics and dropout analyses. They directly test initialization, sensitivity to the dual learning rate, and adaptation to deliberately mismatched symmetries, addressing important questions about ACE's optimization controls and flexibility.

E5.justification: The seed counts remain five for ModelNet40, N-Body, and QM9, and three for CMU MoCap. The added ablation table continues the existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or explicit increase in repetitions is reported.

E6.justification: The retained benchmark and runtime tables are numerically unchanged. New Table 3 reports initialization-ablation MSEs of 4.97±0.01 for gamma=1 and 5.39±0.33 for gamma=0, versus 6.64±0.14 without ACE, all ×10^-3, plus learning-rate sensitivity results. Figure 8 adds qualitative symmetry-correction outcomes. These are additional results, not revisions to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorems 4.1–4.2, the refined appendix bounds, and their derivations are retained. The proofs move from Appendices A.1–A.2 to A.6–A.7. The spectral-normalization discussion explains enforcement of an existing boundedness assumption rather than revising the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive equivariance, partial symmetries, theoretical bounds, and empirical benefits. The new appendix evidence supports these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of initialization versus exploration and practical learning-rate selection, and explains how non-equivariant branch scaling can undermine gamma-based control. It also explicitly cautions that its 300-point ModelNet40 results are not directly comparable with the original 1,024-point VN-DGCNN results. Most existing limitations are merely relocated.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through implementation pseudocode, spectral-normalization and checkpoint-selection guidance, and disclosure of ModelNet40 input resolution and tuning scope. Appendix A.9 replaces v1's promise of code upon acceptance with a stated public repository and reproduction instructions; repository accessibility was not independently checked.

R1.justification: v2 adds the spectral-normalization reference by Miyato et al. and locally distinguishes its C4 toy construction from the already-cited relaxed group-convolution work. The main related-work discussion and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains research-question-based subsections and descriptive paragraph headings. The existing limitations move into the main text, the appendix is reorganized around new explanatory sections, and acknowledgements and the conference footer are added. Most existing prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel ablation Table 3, the C4 example in Figure 8, and formatted code listings. Existing figures and tables are retained with relocation, renumbering, and page reflow rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added ablations and controlled symmetry-mismatch example strengthen practical support for ACE, while input-resolution disclosure, scale-control guidance, and stated code availability improve transparency. The gains are incremental, with the principal results and theory retained. Reproducibility benefits are also qualified by inconsistencies in the new resilient pseudocode, including an extra -u*slack term absent from the stated objective (PII).
